messages:
customer-support: FYI we just got an escalated call from Acme about repeated 503s for hosted inference between 10:12-10:18 UTC. They see request_id=rq_8f7a2c in logs. Customer reports increased QPS (burst to ~950 req/s) and a spike in failures + latency.
ryan-sre: Copy — any stack traces or runner logs attached?
customer-support: Pasted the relevant lines from gateway logs here:
```
2026-03-17T10:12:43Z ERROR upstream: runner exited code=143 signal=TERM pid=2345 model=gpt-small-quantized req_id=rq_8f7a2c
2026-03-17T10:12:43Z WARN watcher: preempted by node-termination instance=host-77
2026-03-17T10:12:44Z ERROR gateway: upstream 503 for req=rq_8f7a2c route=/v1/generate
2026-03-17T10:12:47Z ERROR runner: OOM when allocating 2.1GB for attention_kv cache
```
maria-eng: Interesting — exit code 143 is SIGTERM, but we also see an OOM line in the runner. Could be preemption during eviction causing incomplete cleanup and then OOM on restart.
ajay-ml: Which model size? gateway shows model=gpt-small-quantized but quantization + high sequence length + QPS spike can still push memory. Any per-request seq_len?
customer-support: Customer sent example payload: sequence_length=1024, batch_size=1, stream=false. They said they ramped traffic as part of a product demo.
ryan-sre: Ok repro hypothesis: rapid QPS + long seqs -> KV growth -> host-level preemption (spot/scale events) -> runner restarts + cold cache -> temporary memory pressure -> OOM and 503s. Steps I'm running: 1) check node preemption history 2) gather host dmesg / kube events 3) check autoscaler logs.
sofia-support: Customer is asking for ETA and whether this will incur billing credits. They saw ~12 minutes of errors and want to know cause.
julia-prod: For immediate mitigation, we can: 1) enable fallback routing to lower-memory model (gpt-small-fp16) 2) temporarily cap max seq_len via request filtering 3) throttle the customer's burst via rate limit. I can push a canary for fallback routing. Need signoff.
maria-eng: Also suggest we add a runner-side guard: if process receives SIGTERM while KV allocation > X, attempt async writeout/drop caches and exit gracefully to avoid mid-restart OOMs. Will open an RFC but not immediate.
ryan-sre: Actions: - julia will enable fallback routing for Acme (rate limit fallback + model downgrade) - I will pull node termination events and attach kube evictions. - ajay can run a quick local repro with seq_len=1024 @ 1k qps against quantized runner image to validate memory curve. - support to own customer comms and billing triage.
customer-support: Thanks. Customer wants a clear postmortem and whether usage overage triggers credits.
sofia-support: I'll draft an incident update to Acme: cause = preemptions + memory pressure during high-QPS with long sequences; mitigation = fallback routing enabled, we suggest reducing max seq_len, and we'll follow up with a permanent fix. Marking high priority for billing review.
ajay-ml: Repro steps I used locally (shared):
```bash
# run locust or simple loadgen to hit hosted endpoint via staging key
python loadgen.py --qps 1000 --seq 1024 --duration 5m --endpoint https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate --api-key xxxxx
```
Observations: after ~60s memory climbs, KV cache spikes, one runner gets OOM then restarted, client gets 503s for ~30-90s while autoscaler evicts/recreates.
ryan-sre: I've attached kube events (pasted):
```
Mar 17 10:11:59 KubeController: Node host-77 marked for termination (spot reclaim)
Mar 17 10:12:01 kubelet: Evicting pods: preempted for node termination
Mar 17 10:12:42 runner-pod: Received SIGTERM, exit code 143
```
ryan-sre: Conclusion: root cause is spot/preempt node termination during high-memory workload causing runner restart + cold cache which in combination with high QPS led to transient OOMs and 503s.
maria-eng: Recommended medium-term fixes: 1) avoid scheduling hot runners on preemptible nodes for customers with high SLAs 2) improve graceful shutdown path to flush/compact KV cache on SIGTERM 3) autoscaler tuning to drain slower and allow warm handoff.
sofia-support: I'll share a customer-facing timeline and planned fixes. Billing/cs to confirm credits.
julia-prod: Done — fallback routing enabled for Acme, rate limit set to 300 rps burst 400. Monitoring alert created for any further 5xx spike.
customer-support: Customer acknowledged, will wait for follow-up. Thanks team :handshake:
